requirements.title: Manage ERP-owned supplier entities as commercial counterparties.
acceptance_criteria: Supplier is an ERP-owned commercial entity, separate from CRM and the canonical LoopDev Product master.
Supplier kind supports both companies/organizations and individuals who provide services.

The supplier master captures legal identity, jurisdiction-appropriate tax data, role-based contacts and addresses, purchasing defaults, finance references, and verified payee instructions needed by downstream purchase-to-pay modules.
Supplier tax and bank data are visible to the same user profiles that can access Products through a Supplier-specific read grant; Products catalog.read is not broadened.
Supplier management maps to the Products writer population, with organization-scoped server authorization and auditable changes.
Responsive desktop and mobile web are in scope; native iOS and Android apps are excluded.

requirements.title: Maintain supplier master data ready for purchasing, receiving and future supplier payment.
acceptance_criteria: The Supplier master supports jurisdiction-aware legal/tax identity, role-based contacts and addresses, purchasing defaults, company-specific Finance references, and payee/payment instructions.
Tax and bank fields are viewable by the same profiles that can access Products through a Supplier-specific read grant; changes are auditable and organization-scoped.
Only owner/admin can verify payee instructions, and the verifier differs from the editor; a material account change clears verification.
Initial tax jurisdictions are Spain, the United States and Colombia; Finance/Legal must validate exact country-specific required fields before tax-profile implementation.
Real tax/bank values use protected server-authoritative storage and are unavailable to offline reads, edits or queues.

requirements.title: Bring supplier-provided product and service catalog entries into LoopDev Products.
acceptance_criteria: One supplier may offer many catalog items and one LoopDev item may be linked to multiple suppliers.
Supplier-specific identifiers remain separate from LoopDev's canonical product identity and SKU.
Users can link a supplier item to an existing LoopDev Product or its variant, or initiate Product creation through the Products owner flow.

SupplierItem records can store purchasing UOM/conversion and supplier offer terms such as price/currency, minimum quantity, lead time and validity; selected values are snapshotted by a future purchase order.
Unlinked SupplierItem drafts are not eligible for purchase; a purchasable offer links to a same-organization Product/variant and has a positive purchase-to-stock conversion.
CSV import is excluded from this slice; any later import requires separate scope approval.

requirements.title: Connect Supplier master data to separate purchase-to-pay transaction workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Procurement, Inventory and Finance own purchase orders, actual receipts/stock movements, supplier invoices/payables and payments as separate transaction records.

Downstream transactions reference Supplier and, where applicable, SupplierItem; they snapshot selected defaults/offer terms and retain their own quantities, dates, warehouse, tax, invoice and settlement history.
The Supplier profile never stores per-order, actual-receipt, invoice or payment history as mutable master fields.

capabilities.name: ERP supplier directory

semantics.validation_contract: Require active membership and derive organization from authenticated context. kind, legalName and countryCode are required. Exact tax-identifier duplicates within the same organization and jurisdiction return duplicate; normalized-name similarity warns without auto-merging. Mutations require expectedVersion. Preserve referenced history and do not hard-delete.

capabilities.name: Supplier purchase-to-pay master setup

semantics.validation_contract: Validate tax identifiers and required fields by jurisdiction and supplier kind; initial jurisdictions are Spain, the United States and Colombia, with exact fields blocked on Finance/Legal validation. Recheck expectedVersion and same-organization finance references. Persist mutations only with an audit event; owner/admin verifier must differ from editor.
